"''Agent, victory and defeat are often determined by the smallest detail.|Governor Arihnda Pryce, Agent Alexsandr Kallus, and Grand Admiral [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo|Thrawn]]|{{Rebels|An Inside Man}}}} A '''starfighter''', also referred to as a '''fighter''', was a small and maneuverable [[Starship|spacecraft]] designed for combat in the [[atmosphere]] or [[Realspace|space]]. Certain models of [[bomber]]s, [[gunship]]s, [[transport]]s, [[light freighter]]s, [[shuttle]]s, [[Trainer (starship)|trainers]], and [[atmospheric fighter]]s could be considered starfighters as well, and often fulfilled many of the same functions. Although the term was most commonly applied to starships, it could also include certain low-altitude [[airspeeder]]s. ==Classifications== [[File:BTL-B_Y-wing_BF2.png|thumb|left|250px|Y-wings were considered both bombers and fighters.]] Starfighters often had some degree of overlap with other ship classes, as well as a few distinct sub-classes. [[Bomber]]s were starships designed to carry heavy ordnance payloads, often at the expense of maneuverability and straight-line speed. [[Interceptor]]s represented a range of starfighters that usually emphasized speed and agility over versatility and firepower, sometimes at the expense of ordnance payloads, life support, or hyperdrive capabilities. [[Gunship]]s were heavily-armed vehicles designed to deploy ground forces in landing zones created by their heavy weaponry. Their heavy armament often granted them considerable air-to-air or space-to-space combat capabilities, despite being optimized for air-to-ground combat.{{SWE|technology|droid-gunship|droid gunship}}''[[Star Wars: Commander]]'' All starships that could be deployed from the Starship Command were identified as starfighters in-game. Among these were the [[Low Altitude Assault Transport/infantry]], [[HWK-290 light freighter]], [[E-50 Landseer]], and [[Y-45 armored transport hauler]]. Certain classes of starfighters could be modified to [[Trainer (starship)|trainers]] while still retaining combat capability.{{Rebels|Visions and Voices}} These included certain classes of [[transport]]s, [[shuttle]]s,''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]''. [[LMTR-20]] was identified as a "shuttle" during the film, and was designated as a [[UT-60D U-wing starfighter/support craft]]. and [[light freighter]]s.{{Film|VI}} During the Battle of Endor briefing scene, [[Gial Ackbar]] stated that the fighters would fly into the [[DS-2 Death Star II Mobile Battle Station]] to destroy the reactor core. Since the ''[[Millennium Falcon]]'' flew into the Death Star, it is indirectly identified as a starfighter. ==Characteristics== [[File:PoeDameroncomic-reveal-cover.jpg|thumb|right|300px|A starfighter was controlled by a pilot within a cockpit]] The primary weapon for most starfighters were [[laser cannon]]s, but these could be supplemented with additional weaponry such as [[proton torpedo launcher]]s to provide additional firepower. Often these were effective against other starfighters and similar targets, but didn't have the firepower to punch through the defenses of a [[capital ship]] as during the [[Battle of Naboo]].{{Film|I}} However, some starfighters, like the [[A/SF-01 B-wing starfighter]] carried sufficient armaments that they could destroy capital ships on their own.''[[Rebel Starfighters Owners' Workshop Manual]]'' Starfighters could also cause tremendous devastation when working in groups: a squadron of [[BTL Y-wing starfighter|Y-wing]] bombers were capable of carrying enough ordnance to glass an entire city, bathing the battlefield in blinding white detonations which scrambled enemy sensors.[[Alphabet Squadron (novel)|''Alphabet Squadron'']] Many starfighters were equipped with [[deflector shield]]s to protect them from enemy fire, [[radiation]], and micrometeor impacts. Typically they carried a single [[deflector shield generator]], which could be adjusted to protect specific parts of the starfighter.''[[YT-1300 Millennium Falcon Owners' Workshop Manual]]'' Some starfighters though, notably the [[Eta-2 Actis-class light interceptor]] and [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter]] series, were not equipped with shields, relying instead on their maneuverability and the pilot's skills to avoid these dangers.''[[TIE Fighter Owners' Workshop Manual]]'' Other common forms of protection included heavy armor plating and [[sensor jammer]]s.''[[Rebel Starfighters Owners' Workshop Manual]]'' Starfighters were equipped with warning systems to let them know when an enemy missile was locked on to them, and could also use their laser cannons to shoot these down, even against missiles traveling at incomprehensible speeds, so long as their [[targeting computer]] was functional.''[[Shadow Fall: An Alphabet Squadron Novel]]'' Some starfighters were equipped with a [[hyperdrive]], whether integral to the craft itself or by means of external attachment such as a [[hyperspace transport ring]]. Because of their small size, most starfighter [[navigation computer]]s or navicomputers could only carry one or two hyperspace routes which either had to be pre-programmed into the computer or installed via removable [[datachip]]s (for emergency jumps, navicomputers could also receive coordinates transmitted from friendly ships). This made [[astromech droid]]s a valuable addition to many starfighters in that they had the storage capacity to carry up to ten hyperspace coordinates. [[File:FrontLines-OddBall.png|thumb|left|300px|Starfighters engaged in space combat]] A starfighter's primary means of propulsion were [[sublight engine]]s which allowed it to get clear of a planet's atmosphere and gravitation field in a matter of minutes and cross vast distances of [[realspace]].''[[Star Wars: The Visual Encyclopedia]]'' Though small, these sublight drives were capable of accelerating starfighters at thousands of times standard [[gravity]]. To protect their pilots from being killed by the G-force generated by sublight drives, starfighters were equipped with [[acceleration compensator]]s. These compensators were designed to automatically adjust their settings during flight, but if this function became disabled a pilot could find themselves subject to potentially dangerous g-forces.''[[Victory's Price: An Alphabet Squadron Novel]]'' During space combat, starfighters flew and fought at speeds which would be incomprehensible in an atmosphere, crossing thousands of kilometers in a matter of minutes. Only the vastness of space and the relative speeds of those involved made flying at such velocities fathomable for many pilots. Even then, computer assistance was necessary for accurate piloting, as having a starfighter's vectoring be wrong by one degree could easily result in it being kilometers off-target. Some starfighters like the [[A-wing starfighter|A-wing]] were so fast and maneuverable that, because they lacked an astromech droid to assist with flying, even a being with [[Jedi]]-like reflexes found them challenging to pilot. Starfighters flying in tight formations relied on close communications between their navicomputers and astromech droids to maintain perfect distance. [[File:TIE_Striker_-_Fathead_-_Rogue_One.png|thumb|right|240px|The TIE/sk x1 experimental air superiority fighter was an atmospheric fighter that was capable of starfighter operations.]] For atmospheric flight and during landings and takeoffs, starfighters carried [[repulsorlift]] engines as a secondary means of propulsion. Because sublight engines' exhaust was hot and mildly radioactive, using them while inside an inhabited world's atmosphere was generally illegal. When the need was dire though a starfighter could use their sublight engines for extra speed during atmospheric flight, even flying at maximum acceleration as during the [[Battle of Pandem Nai|attack on Pandem Nai]]. While starfighters could function in an atmosphere at such speeds, it put tremendous strain on the ships and the pilots themselves. Systems would start to fail after just several minutes of such velocities, and laser cannons were at risk of melting from the heat generated by these maneuvers. Starfighters equipped with deflector shields could use them help smooth their passage through and allow for greater control when operating in an atmosphere. Deflector shields could also allow starfighters, like the [[Aggressive ReConnaissance-170 starfighter|ARC-170]] and [[Alpha-3 Nimbus-class V-wing starfighter|V-wing]] to achieve hypersonic velocities in an atmosphere.''[[Ultimate Star Wars, New Edition]]'' However, most starfighters were not built to excel at atmospheric flight, and were at a disadvantage against [[airspeeder]]s when flying below [[mountain]] range as they were forced to sacrifice their superior speed.''[[Star Wars Complete Vehicles, New Edition]]'' Exceptions to this included the [[X-wing starfighter|X-wing]] and [[TIE/sk x1 experimental air superiority fighter]], the latter of which was classified as an [[atmospheric fighter]],''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: The Ultimate Visual Guide]]'' yet it also functioned as a starfighter.{{FFGXW|set=TIE Striker Expansion Pack|cardname=Imperial Trainee}} ==History== ===Early years=== Starfighters had been an integral part of [[Realspace|space]]-based combat for [[Millennium|millennia]], seeing action as early as the [[Standard day|days]] of the [[Galactic Republic|Old Republic]].{{TCW|Citadel Rescue}} However, with the formation of the modern Galactic Republic and the millennium of relative peace that followed,{{Film|II}} large-scale battles between opposing space-based combatants were completely unheard of. ===Invasion of Naboo and Separatist Crisis=== {{Quote|Fighters, straight ahead.|[[Ric Olié]] during the [[Battle of Naboo]]|}} [[File:N-1_vs_Vulture_droid.png|thumb|left|250px|An N-1 starfighter firing on a Vulture droid.]] In [[32 BBY]], the [[Jedi Order]] operated the [[Delta-7 Aethersprite-class light interceptor|Delta-7 ''Aethersprite''-class light interceptor]], but primarily used them for personal transport instead of space combat.[[Star Wars (2015) 26|''Star Wars'' (2015) 26]] That year, [[N-1 starfighter]]s of the [[Naboo Royal Space Fighter Corps]] engaged and defeated the [[Trade Federation]]'s [[Vulture-class starfighter|''Vulture''-class starfighters]] during the latter's [[invasion of Naboo]].{{Film|I}} A number of N-1s remained combat capable all the way through the end of the [[Cold War]].''[[Star Wars Battlefront II]]'' The Vulture droids also had a long lifespan, with some remaining operational in the [[Imperial Era|Age of the Empire]].''[[Lords of the Sith]]'' Also around that time, [[Maul|Darth Maul]] operated the ''[[Scimitar]]'', a customized [[Star Courier]] that was also a formidable starfighter. It remained in service of the [[Sith]] Order well into the Imperial era. Towards the end of the Separatist Crisis, [[Jango Fett]] owned and operated ''[[Slave I]]'', a customized [[Firespray-31-class patrol and attack craft|''Firespray-31''-class patrol and attack craft]]. After his death at the [[First Battle of Geonosis]], his son [[Boba Fett|Boba]] took possession of the ship and continued using it until at least [[9 ABY]].{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 14: The Tragedy}} ===Clone Wars=== During the Clone Wars, the [[Jedi]] continued utilizing the old Delta-7s, but also developed the [[Delta-7B Aethersprite-class light interceptor|Delta-7B ''Aethersprite''-class light interceptor]][[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (film)|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' film]] and [[Eta-2 Actis-class light interceptor|Eta-2 ''Actis''-class light interceptor]].{{Film|III}} The [[clone trooper pilot]]s under their [[Commanding officer|command]] flew [[Low Altitude Assault Transport/infantry]] gunships, [[V-19 Torrent starfighter]]s, [[BTL Y-wing starfighter]]s,{{TCW|Shadow of Malevolence|Shadow of ''Malevolence''}} [[Aggressive ReConnaissance-170 starfighter]]s, [[Clone Z-95 starfighter|Clone Z-95 Headhunters]],{{TCW|Darkness on Umbara}} and [[Alpha-3 Nimbus-class V-wing starfighter|Alpha-3 ''Nimbus''-class V-wing starfighters]]. [[Grand Master]] [[Yoda]] operated [[Yoda's fighter|his own]] customized ''Actis''-class fighter.{{TCW|Voices}} [[Skull Squadron]], a [[Mandalorian]] unit serving the Republic, flew [[Fang-class Protectorate fighter|Fang fighters]].[[Kanan 10|''Kanan'' 10]] At the conclusion of the Clone War, some of the Republic starfighter classes would be inherited by the [[Galactic Empire]], while others would be decommissioned and fall into the hands of the rebellion. Others would be discarded entirely, seeing almost no military service after the conclusion of the war. [[File:Vultures_Teth.png|thumb|right|250px|Vulture droids were major starfighters operated by the Confederacy.]] The [[Confederacy of Independent Systems|Separatists]], which opposed the Republic in the Clone War, mainly used ''Vulture''-class [[droid starfighter]]s built for the Trade Federation. Later, to counter increasingly capable and diverse clone fighters, the Confederacy manufactured and deployed [[droid tri-fighter]]s, [[Hyena-class Droid Fighter/Bomber|''Hyena''-class Droid Bombers]],{{TCW|Cat and Mouse}} and [[HMP droid gunship]]s. The Separatists also built manned fighters for their organic commanders, such as [[Rogue-class Porax-38 starfighter|''Rogue''-class Porax-38 starfighters]], [[Belbullab-22 heavy starfighter]]s, and [[Ginivex-class fanblade starfighter|''Ginivex''-class fanblade starfighter]].{{TCW|Nightsisters (episode)}} [[Geonosian]] forces, which allied themselves with the Confederacy, flew [[Nantex-class territorial defense starfighter|''Nantex''-class territorial defense starfighters]], while the [[Umbaran Militia]] flew their indigenous [[Zenuas 33 Umbaran starfighter]]s. The [[Zygerrian Slave Empire]], which allied itself with the Confederacy, had a small force of [[Hutt]]ese [[HH-87 Starhopper]]s, which saw action against Republic forces on [[Kadavo]].{{TCW|Escape from Kadavo}} [[Death Watch]], a Mandalorian splinter group allied to the Confederacy, operated [[Kom'rk-class fighter/transport|''Kom'rk''-class fighter/transports]], which doubled as transports and bombers.{{TCW|The Mandalore Plot}} After falling out of [[Count]] [[Dooku]]'s favor, Death Watch would pledge their loyalty to Darth Maul's [[Shadow Collective]], but would continue to use the ships in battle.[[Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir 1|''Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir'' 1]] After the conclusion of the war, many of the starfighters used by the Confederacy's regular forces survived the Clone War and were used by rebels fighting against the Empire.[[Tarkin (novel)|''Tarkin'']] ===Age of the Empire and Rebellion=== {{Quote|We'll have to destroy them ship to ship. Get the crews to their fighters.|Darth Vader during the Battle of Yavin|{{Film|IV}}}} At the conclusion of the Clone War, the [[Imperial Military]] inherited some of the starfighter classes of the [[Republic Navy]]. By the time of the Galactic Civil War, however, it was reliant on the [[TIE series|TIE fighter series]]. This new generation of vehicles, powered by [[twin ion engine]]s, were developed from technology used in the older Republic starfighter and transport classes. These craft included the famous [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter]], [[TIE/rb heavy starfighter]],''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story]]'' [[TIE/ad v1]],{{Rebels|Empire Day (episode)}} [[TIE/sa tactical bomber|TIE/sa bomber]],{{Film|V}} [[TIE Advanced x1]], [[TIE/IN interceptor]],{{Film|VI}} [[TIE/d "Defender" Multi-Role Starfighter]],{{Rebels|Secret Cargo}} [[TIE/sk x1 experimental air superiority fighter]], and [[TIE/rp Reaper attack lander]].''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'' The Empire also deployed [[VT-49 Decimator]]s and [[Y-45 armored transport hauler]]s. In addition to Imperial use, numerous TIE/LNs were given to the [[Mining Guild]] and converted to [[TIE/mg Mining Guild starfighter]]s.''[[Star Wars Rebels: Steps Into Shadow]]'' Imperial TIEs would occasionally fall into rebel hands, and the rebellion made good use of these opportunities.{{Rebels|Fighter Flight}}{{Rebels|Fire Across the Galaxy}} Out of desperation for any equipment they could obtain, the rebellion operated numerous starfighter classes from a variety of sources. [[Bail Prestor Organa|Bail Organa's]] rebel network operated [[RZ-1 A-wing interceptor]]s as early as [[18 BBY]].[[Ahsoka (novel)|''Ahsoka'']] The [[Free Ryloth Movement]] used old Separatist droid starfighters in [[14 BBY]]. [[Berch Teller's rebel cell]] also used Separatist fighters, in addition to [[Z-95 Headhunter]]s. Beginning around [[5 BBY]],the [[Spectres]] made use of the ''[[Phantom]]'', a customized [[Corellian]] [[VCX-series auxiliary starfighter]] that doubled as a shuttle and scout craft. The Spectres eventually joined [[Phoenix Cell]], which utilized A-wings and a small number of [[RZ-1T trainer]]s, which were A-wings converted into two-seat trainers. [[Massassi Group|Jan Dodonna's unit]] made use of decommissioned Republic Y-wings, which served as multi-role fighter-bombers. Later, the loose-knit network of rebel cells morphed into the better-organized Alliance to Restore the Republic, which continued to operate a fairly ragtag collection of whatever equipment they could acquire.''[[Star Wars Rebels]]'' [[File:Yavin_dogfight.png|thumb|left|250px|TIEs and X-wings became symbols of the Empire and Rebellion.]] The [[Rebel Alliance Starfighter Corps]] made use of [[A/SF-01 B-wing starfighter]]s, [[E-50 Landseer]]s, converted [[HWK-290 light freighter]]s, [[T-47 airspeeder]]s, [[T-65B X-wing starfighter]]s, [[T-65C-A2 X-wing starfighter]]s,''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: The Ultimate Visual Guide]]'' [[UT-60D U-wing starfighter/support craft]], [[V-4X-D ski speeder]]s, and at least one [[YT-1300 light freighter]], in addition to some of the older classes. Additionally, the rebellion made use of stolen Imperial vessels. Many starfighter types used by the various rebel groups continued to see action with the [[New Republic]].[[Aftermath (novel)|''Aftermath'']] A number of starfighter classes were used by private security forces, such as the [[Storm IV Twin-Pod cloud car]]s used by the [[Bespin Wing Guard]]. ===Post-Endor=== {{Quote|I have my own way of fighting. Not everything is about armadas and starfighters, you know.|[[Maz Kanata]], to Resistance Commander [[Poe Dameron]]|''[[Resistance Reborn]]''}} In its early days, the New Republic continued to operate the rebellion's old starfighter classes, and even continued stealing TIEs when the need arose. Beginning in [[5 ABY]], the New Republic operated the [[T-70 X-wing starfighter]],''[[Aftermath: Empire's End]]'' which was an upgraded version of the T-65. They also operated [[RZ-2 A-wing interceptor]]s. By the time of the cold war, the [[New Republic Defense Fleet]] had retired all of the older starfighter classes (as well as some of the newer ones, such as the [[B-wing Mark II]]) in favor of the [[T-85 X-wing starfighter|T-85 X-wing]].''[[Before the Awakening]]'' [[File:TIE_Silencer.png|thumb|right|300px|The TIE silencer was considered the ultimate evolution of the TIE design.]] The [[First Order Navy]] continued the TIE line that the Empire had begun, with the new models upgraded to modern combat standards. This new generation of TIEs included the [[TIE/fo space superiority fighter]], the two-seat [[TIE/sf space superiority fighter]] used by the [[First Order Special Forces]], and the [[TIE/vn space superiority fighter]] used by [[Ben Solo|Kylo Ren]].{{StarWarsShow|tMTExpDs7WA|Kylo Ren's New Ship, The Last Jedi Cast at D23, & Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge!|sw_url=video/kylo-ren-s-new-ship-the-last-jedi-cast-at-d23-and-star-wars-galaxy-s-edge}} The [[TIE/wi Interceptor]] and [[TIE/wi modified interceptor]] would also come to exist.{{Film|IX}} Meanwhile, the [[Resistance]]'s [[Resistance Starfighter Corps|Starfighter Corps]] continued using T-70s donated by sympathetic [[New Republic Senate|senators]].{{Film|VII}} They also made use of a small number of single-seat A-wings''[[Star Wars: Poe Dameron]]''{{Film|VIII}} and a few Z-95 Headhunters for covert operations.
